params.body:
Shane reported on staging, on cutover day: "blurren ongedaan maken" on a platform photo leaves a grey, empty tile. The neighbour still renders, so the gallery is fine; that one image is gone. Finding X-127, rule R S1-6.27.

## What actually happened

"Undo the blur" is `ImageController::removeBg` with `redo=1`, which dispatches `ProcessImage($id, duplicate: true, removeBg: true, blur: false)`: copy the dealer's original again, cut the background out again, no blur. Two defects in that job, reproduced against the original code with a locally faked remove.bg (`Http::fake`; nothing left the machine) and in a running application against a local S3 emulator:

1. **The row moved before the file.** With `duplicate`, the job first assigned the row a fresh path (`stocklist_car_image_0(1).jpg`, the next free name) and saved it, and only then copied, behind `if (exists(source))`. When the original is not in the bucket (the media migration stopped halfway, so this is common on staging), nothing was copied, the row pointed at a file that was never written, nothing threw (so `failed()` never ran), `processing` went to 0 and the dealer saw no change at all. Every retry picked the next free name with the same result.
2. **The row promised derived sizes that did not exist.** After a real remove.bg run, `old_remove_background` wrote the new `trans_path` (`stocklist_car_image_0(1).png`) onto the row, but `media_version` stayed what it was. `VehicleImageService::url` then builds a signed bucket URL for `_afgeleid/{new trans_path}/{old version}-sm.webp`, an object nobody made. The bucket answers 403 (404 on the emulator) and the tile is grey, even though the photo itself is on disk. The local fake path did set a version, which is why this never showed on a developer machine.

The row Shane looked at had both: a `path` pointing at nothing and a URL pointing at a derived size that was never written.

## What protects the existing photo now

- `ProcessImage::dupliceer()` writes the new file, reads it back, and only then repoints the row. The old file is never overwritten or deleted (a copy always gets a fresh name). If the original is missing, the row is left exactly as it was: same path, same blurred version, same media version.
- `ProcessImage::nieuweMediaVersie()` is the one place that sets `media_version`: it warms the derived sizes of what lies on disk now and sets the version only when that succeeded; otherwise it clears the version so every URL falls back to the plain file (slower, but visible). The Blurit webhook keeps writing its own version afterwards, as before.
- `PlatformPhotoService::duplicate` and `ImageController::duplicate_image` no longer copy the original's `media_version`/`media_set` onto a fresh copy: those belong to the original's path.
- A photo with no original to copy from (an own photo, `vehicle_photo_id` empty) is processed on its own path instead of throwing a TypeError on `exists(null)`.

## What the dealer sees on failure

The spinner stops and the tile carries a red strip: "Niet gelukt. De oorspronkelijke foto staat niet meer op de server." or "Niet gelukt. De beeldverwerking gaf geen resultaat terug." (nl/en/fr/de; es falls back to en as the other `ui.*` keys do), with "De foto is ongewijzigd gebleven. Probeer het opnieuw." as the tooltip. The photo underneath is the one they had. The reason is cleared at the start of every new attempt, so a tile that is processing never says "failed". `failed()` (Blurit refused, queue gave up) notes the same reason instead of leaving `processing = 1` forever.

## Can a broken row recover?

Yes, by clicking again. A row the old code left with `path` pointing at nothing recovers as soon as the original is in the bucket: the job copies it to a fresh name, repoints the row and sets a version that matches what is on disk (test `test_a_row_that_already_points_at_nothing_recovers_when_the_original_is_there`; the recovered tile is in the screenshots). If the original is gone too, the tile says so and keeps whatever file it still has. Only a platform copy with no file at all (no original, no blurred version) is hard-deleted, the same rule `failed()` already applied (R S1-6.26): it then counts as missing again and the next save or `stocklist:platformfotos` makes it anew. A row with a `path` to nothing but a visible `trans_path` is explicitly kept: that is a photo the dealer can see.

## Migration decision: none

The previous draft added `vehicle_photos.processing_error` (nullable string) plus a `language_lines` migration. Both are dropped.

- The reason is transient by nature: it is true only until the next attempt, which clears it first, and a week later it says nothing about the photo. A column would have been a schema change on `vehicle_photos` on the day the production dump is imported into the new box, to be run before and after the import. Not worth it for a fact that expires. It lives in the cache instead (`App\Support\PhotoFailure`: key `photo-failure:{id}`, a translation key, seven days), which already exists, survives from the queue worker to the dealer's browser, and forgets by itself. The price: a `cache:clear` drops the labels, and the tile is then plain, which is exactly today's behaviour. If the reason ever has to be reported on (how often does remove.bg refuse, per dealer), that is the moment for a column; noted as an open point in the class docblock.
- The translations migration was wrong for this repo regardless: the Spatie DB loader was replaced by the stock file loader (`config/app.php`), so the four keys go in `resources/lang/{nl,en,fr,de}/ui.php` next to `unblur_confirm`.

So: no schema change, nothing to sequence with `CUTOVER.md`, and the branch is safe to deploy before or after the dump import.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/ProcessImageKeepsPhotoTest` (7 tests, `@rule S1-6.27` and `S1-6.26`): original missing keeps file and row and notes the reason; new file exists before the row points at it, old file untouched, derived sizes exist at the new version for both path and trans_path; a row pointing at nothing recovers; a row with only its blurred file is kept and labelled; a copy with no file at all is removed; an own photo is processed on its own path; a new attempt clears the previous reason.

`php artisan test --filter='Photo|Image|ProcessImage|PlatformPhoto|OwnStock|Outbound|RulesCoverage|CompiledViews'`: 98 tests, 413 assertions, 0 failures (the "warnings" are the worktree's missing `.env` being read). `bin/rules-coverage` exit 0.

Reproduced in a running application (PHP built-in server, MySQL from the schema, a local S3 emulator so the tile URLs are real signed bucket URLs; remove.bg via `Http::fake`, never the real service): before, tile 1 grey with its neighbours intact and tile 0 silently unchanged with its row pointing at a missing file; after, tile 0 keeps its photo with the label and tile 1 is back.
params.title: Removing the blur left an empty tile
